To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
creatine supplementation can be used to induce transitions to slower myosin heavy chains (MHCs) in juvenile rats but that this effect is not observed in adult animals.
the age of animals is a critical variable in the design of studies involving creatine depletion.
creatine depletion results in a shift toward expression of slow myosin heavy chains in rat skeletal muscle and this shift is age dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulation of muscle phenotype in the adult animal, and the results presented in this paper indicate that the creatine analogue, beta-guanidino-propionic acid, can be used to induce MHC isoform transitions in adult animals.
the role of creatine in regulating the expression of myosin isozyme genes in skeletal muscle.
the regulation of myosin isozymes in skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the age-dependent effects of beta-guanidino-propionic acid on myosin heavy-chain isoform expression in skeletal muscle are not a function of creatine depletion per se but rather a function of the age of the animal.
there is an age-dependent effect of creatine deprivation on MHC isoform transitions in skeletal muscles.
creatine depletion in juvenile animals induces a significant shift in MHC isoform distribution toward slower MHC isoform content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the creatine analogue-induced myosin transitions are an age-dependent phenomenon.
the age of the animal at the time of creatine depletion is critical for the expression of myosin transitions.
the effects of creatine depletion (or supplementation) on MHC transitions in skeletal muscle is an age-dependent phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of creatine depletion are different in adult and juvenile rats.
the use of creatine analogues to study MHC transitions should take into account the age of the animals to be used, because the results of such studies may be dependent on animal age.
creatine depletion is a useful tool to induce MHC transitions, but only when used with juvenile animals.
